room_thesis: The swarm - every member either hits many times or protects the one that does.
cap_window_confirmation: Authored offsets 2/2/1/2/2/6 resolved to 42/42/41/42/42/46, i.e. cap 42 + offset - 2 on Medium; the driver reported level_cap 42. Cap 42 is correct for every Petalburg Gym room: Norman's Balance Badge is what raises the cap to 48 and it is awarded at the END of this Gym, so 48 applies only to encounters after play_order 145.
pre_declared_strategy_checks: Maushold takes Follow Me while a partner fires a multi-hit attack into the exposed slot
Ambipom opens with Technician Fake Out rather than being locked out of it
Skill Link fixes Cinccino's hit count at 5 but does NOT fix accuracy, and Population Bomb still misses
Friend Guard reduces damage to Maushold's partner only, not to Maushold

attempts.narrative: The longest and strangest battle in my block: a 6-5 win in which my last surviving Pokemon had no move that could damage anything on the field. I built four Ghosts because the dossier's own crack list leads with Ghost immunity, and the defensive half of that plan worked perfectly - Tail Slap, Double Hit, Fake Out, Body Slam, Double-Edge and Population Bomb are all Normal and all 0x. The offensive half was a construction error I have to own: Ghost STAB is also 0x into Normal, so Shadow Ball on three of my six was a dead move, and Cofagrigus in particular entered the battle unable to deal damage to a single opponent. T1 Will-O-Wisp missed Cinccino, a critical 5-hit Bullet Seed took half of Sableye, and Ambipom's Knock Off - Dark, 2x into Ghost/Steel - stripped Aegislash's Leftovers. Sacred Sword took Cinccino to 2 HP. T2 Ambipom's second Knock Off killed Aegislash in Blade form, and Cinccino killed itself with Life Orb recoil at 2 HP (see defect P12-D7). T3 Fake Out removed Ambipom. T4 Dodrio Protected my Will-O-Wisp on the turn it arrived; T5 the burn landed, Population Bomb hit ten times for 88, and Brave Bird killed Sableye. T6 Flamethrower killed Maushold through its Follow Me, and Knock Off traded Incineroar for Dodrio via Rocky Helmet. T7 a Serene Grace Rock Slide flinched Amoonguss out of a Spore and Greedent's Crunch killed Chandelure. T8-T9 Dunsparce's Serene Grace Body Slam paralysed Amoonguss, which then never moved again and died. From turn 10 the fight was a burned Greedent and a burned Dunsparce against one Cofagrigus that cannot hurt either of them - and Cofagrigus won it, because Body Slam and Population Bomb are 0x into Ghost, Greedent's Crunch was the only super-effective attack left on the field, and once Greedent burned to death Dunsparce had literally no way to deal meaningful damage. Twelve turns of Protect, burn chip and nothing else. That is a real result and it is also the most important design finding in my block.

strategy_checks.check: Maushold Follow Me protecting a multi-hit partner
strategy_checks.evidence: T6: 'The opposing Maushold used Follow Me!' / 'became the center of attention'. It used the move on the turn it was paired with a damaged Dodrio, which is the correct turn. It did not save Maushold - Flamethrower was already aimed at Maushold itself, so the redirection was a no-op against that specific command - but the selection was right and the ability was live.

strategy_checks.check: Ambipom opens with Technician Fake Out
strategy_checks.evidence: Ambipom never used Fake Out in the entire battle. It used Knock Off twice, which was the right call and the reason it was the most effective member on Randall's team: Fake Out is Normal and 0x into both of my Ghost leads, while Knock Off is Dark and 2x into Ghost/Steel Aegislash. The AI recognised that its signature opening move was a complete blank and used the one move on its set that was super-effective instead. This is the single best decision made by any opponent in my block. Recording the authored check as failed but the behaviour as correct - the dossier's expectation ('Ambipom opens with Technician Fake Out instead of being locked out of it') is written for a board that does not contain Ghosts.

strategy_checks.check: Skill Link fixes hit count but not accuracy
strategy_checks.result: PASS on hit count, NOT TESTED on accuracy
strategy_checks.evidence: 'The Pokemon was hit 5 times!' on both of Cinccino's Bullet Seeds and 'hit 10 times' on Maushold's Population Bomb. Neither missed in this sample, so the dossier's honest warning that Population Bomb still misses did not get to bite.

strategy_checks.check: Friend Guard reduces damage to the partner only
strategy_checks.evidence: Maushold was on the field for two turns beside a Dodrio I mostly did not attack, so I have no clean before/after damage comparison. The ability was live on the battler. Recording honestly as not measured rather than claiming a pass.

strategy_checks.check: Serene Grace doubles Dunsparce's secondary effects
strategy_checks.result: PASS, and it decided the middle of the battle
strategy_checks.evidence: Two separate procs in consecutive turns: T7 Rock Slide flinched Amoonguss out of a Spore that would have shut down Dunsparce, and T9 Body Slam paralysed Amoonguss, which then failed to move and died without acting again. A 60 percent flinch and a 60 percent paralysis on the same battler is exactly what Serene Grace is for and the +6 offset on Dunsparce is earned.

Greedent consumed its Sitrus Berry but Cheek Pouch only heals on berry consumption, and it holds one berry; there is no Recycle or Harvest on the set, so 'recycles its own Sitrus' is not something this loadout can actually do more than once. The dossier's prose overstates it - see the legality/accuracy note below.

strategy_checks.check: Multi-hit attacks break Focus Sash and Substitute
strategy_checks.evidence: I brought neither, deliberately - a Sash is worthless against a Skill Link user. The dossier's claim is mechanically obvious and I did not construct a party to verify it.

strategy_checks.check: Every opposing Protect has a payoff
strategy_checks.evidence: Only two opposing Protects in twenty-one turns, both good - see the ledger. Notably, this room did NOT reproduce the consecutive-Protect defect found on Alan's team at play_order 137.

protect_ledger.payoff: EXCELLENT. Dodrio Protected on the first turn it was on the field and blocked a Prankster Will-O-Wisp. Dodrio is the room's fast physical attacker with Brave Bird and Double-Edge, so a burn would have halved its entire purpose; guarding the turn it arrived, when a freshly-switched battler is most exposed, is the right instinct. It cost Randall nothing, because the alternative target was an 8 HP Sableye it could not reach with priority anyway.

N/A - Maushold used Follow Me rather than Protect. Listed here only to record that the room's other guard holder chose redirection over guarding on the turn its partner was the more valuable body, which is the correct use of the pair.

protect_ledger_note: Two guard-class decisions across twenty-one turns from a team with four Protects on it. That is a low rate and the two that happened were correct. No empty guards, no consecutive repeats. Randall's guard cadence is the best in my block so far.

ai_defects.board: Cinccino at 2 of 128 HP, holding a Life Orb, with MOVE_PROTECT on its set. Opponent (me): Sableye at 75/150 and Aegislash in Blade form at 66/141.
ai_defects.why_wrong: Life Orb recoil is 10 percent of the user's maximum HP - 12 HP for this Cinccino - and Cinccino was at 2 HP. Any Life Orb attack it selected was a guaranteed self-KO regardless of what it hit. The log confirms it: 'The opposing Cinccino lost some of its HP!' / 'The opposing Cinccino fainted!' The AI killed its own battler with its own item. This requires no read of my commands at all: the battler's own HP, its own item and its own maximum HP are all self-knowledge.
ai_defects.better_action: MOVE_PROTECT, which is on the set, costs nothing, and would have kept a Skill Link multi-hit attacker alive for at least one more turn.
ai_defects.note: The general shape: the damage-scoring path does not appear to subtract the user's own Life Orb recoil from the value of an attack when that recoil is lethal. This is a shared path - Life Orb appears on a very large number of authored sets, including Ambipom in this same room and Cinccino, Meowstic-F, Chandelure and others across the campaign - so it is worth indexing broadly. It is also the cheapest of my findings to reason about, because it is a pure self-knowledge check with no forecast involved. Not fixed here; the brief forbids editing AI C code in this pass.

ai_defects.board: From turn 10 onward: my Cofagrigus (Ghost, between 62 and 140 HP, alternating Protect and Will-O-Wisp, no damaging move that is not 0x into Normal) against a burned Greedent and a burned Dunsparce.
ai_defects.chosen: Greedent repeatedly selected MOVE_BODY_SLAM into Cofagrigus; Dunsparce repeatedly selected MOVE_BODY_SLAM and MOVE_GLARE into Cofagrigus.
ai_defects.why_wrong: Body Slam is Normal and Cofagrigus is a Ghost: the move deals exactly zero damage and the AI selected it many times across a dozen turns while both battlers burned to death. Greedent had MOVE_CRUNCH on its set - Dark, 2x into Ghost, and the move that had killed my Chandelure three turns earlier - and used Body Slam instead. Dunsparce had MOVE_ROCK_SLIDE, which is 1x rather than 0x. The type chart here is static knowledge, not a forecast; Cofagrigus's type was visible from the moment it entered.
ai_defects.better_action: Greedent: MOVE_CRUNCH every turn. Dunsparce: MOVE_ROCK_SLIDE every turn. Either would have killed Cofagrigus long before the burn killed them.
ai_defects.note: This is the defect that actually decided the battle, and it is much more serious than P12-D7 because the room is a Normal-type Gym: a large fraction of every set in rooms 138, 141, 142, 143 and 144 is Normal-typed, so a player who brings one Ghost wall and one burn source can reproduce this against five of the seven Petalburg rooms. I want to be careful about how I characterise it, because I do not know from the logs whether the AI scored the 0x move as positive or simply had no better-scoring option after some other filter ran. Either way the observable behaviour is that a 0x move was preferred over an available 2x move by the same battler that had already used that 2x move successfully. Recommend the main agent reproduce this specifically with a focused regression - one Ghost, one Normal attacker holding both a Normal STAB and a Dark coverage move - before touching any constants. Not fixed here; the brief forbids editing AI C code in this pass.

ai_notes: Ambipom's refusal to use its signature Fake Out against two Ghosts, in favour of a 2x Knock Off that killed Aegislash, is genuinely impressive play and is the counter-example that makes P12-D8 confusing - the same engine that got Ambipom exactly right got Greedent exactly wrong on the same axis.
Dodrio's turn-of-arrival Protect against a Prankster burn was well judged.

Serene Grace Dunsparce at +6 is the most dangerous single member of the room and the offset is justified by play, not by prose: it flinched and then paralysed my Amoonguss on consecutive turns and removed it from the battle without ever dealing significant damage.
AI decision time peaked at 1.088 s, the highest in my block so far but still inside the 1.2 s budget. The peak came on the six-member opening board, as expected.
calibration: Won on the first optimized attempt, but 5 of 6 player faints and a 21-turn battle. Brief rule 5: won with 2+ faints after a real fight -> keep. No level change, and I would resist one in either direction until P12-D8 is resolved. The room removed five of my six Pokemon, which is exactly the pressure AGENTS.md asks of a Gym trainer; the reason it lost is not that its levels are too low but that two of its members spent twelve turns using a move that could not damage the only target on the field. Fix the AI first, then re-measure. If anything, a room that takes five of six at these levels is priced correctly.
could_this_be_cooler: The concept is excellent and I would not touch the species list - Cinccino, Ambipom, Dodrio, Maushold, Greedent and Dunsparce is a genuinely coherent swarm and the multi-hit identity is real in every slot, exactly as the dossier's own revision note claims. The problem is narrower and more serious than 'could it be cooler': the room has essentially no answer to the counterplay its own dossier names first. Ghost immunity is listed at the top of Randall's crack list, and in practice a single Ghost with a burn move beat the back half of the team unaided. Across all six sets there are exactly two moves that are super-effective against Ghost - Ambipom's Knock Off and Greedent's Crunch - and both sit on members that also want to be doing something else. The specific, minimal improvement I would recommend is to give the room one more Dark or Ghost coverage slot on a member that is not already the team's utility piece, so that the named counterplay is a puzzle rather than a solution. Dodrio is the natural candidate: it carries Brave Bird, Double-Edge and Drill Run, of which Double-Edge is 0x into the exact matchup the dossier tells the player to bring. Second, smaller note: the dossier says Greedent 'recycles its own Sitrus through Cheek Pouch as the attrition answer', but Cheek Pouch only heals when a berry is eaten and the set has no way to get a second berry, so that sentence describes a loop the loadout cannot perform. Worth correcting the prose or giving it the tool. Dunsparce at +6 with Eviolite and Serene Grace is the best-designed member and should not be touched.
legality_problems_in_authored_set: Not a legality problem, but a prose/loadout mismatch: Greedent's plan text claims it 'recycles its own Sitrus through Cheek Pouch'. Cheek Pouch heals on berry consumption and the set holds a single Sitrus with no Recycle, Harvest or second berry, so the recycling loop described cannot occur.
scope: Synthetic headless benchmark through scripts/playthrough/battle_driver.py against work/agent-battle-build-2. Not earned campaign traversal; no story progress awarded.
